_comment: The Grade 4 Science standalone lesson build, described for ../../mathematics/lesson-app-tools and built by ../lesson-kit. Order here IS the lesson number. Thirteen lessons organised by the sub-strands of Cambridge Primary Science 0097 Stage 4 (63 objectives), NOT by the units of the course under science/grade-4/data, so progress is written under l01..l13 - see THE UNIT PROBLEM in wire-progress.py. The shell course was re-pointed from 0846 to 0097 on 2026-09-17, so the two now share a framework and STILL must not share progress keys: six units and thirteen lessons are different partitions of it, and emitting u01 would claim a whole unit was finished by one lesson. The app is also the vehicle that covers Stage 4 in full - the shell course reaches 36 of 63, because its six units are one per sub-strand of the 2018 framework. objectiveFloors are recorded at the measured value after each build and may rise, not fall.
subject: science
_sittings: Two sittings per lesson (Grade 4 validation, area 17): each lesson is cut at the step nearest its halfway point, with a break card. Read by lesson-kit/_shell.py.
_extraPages: The Bones and Muscles unit lecture film, its captions and its poster (tools/create-ehel-science-unit-lecture.js). Lesson 1 names all three in LESSON["video"] and build-lessons.py refuses a path that is not BOTH on disk and listed here, because a deploy only carries what this list names.
hubStrands: Models and their limits, models of scale; the five enquiry types; variables in a fair test; keys; repeated measurements and reliable data; standard units; tables, bar charts and dot plots; patterns and conclusions.

The bones and how muscles move them; skeletons, exoskeletons, vertebrates and invertebrates; medicines, vaccines and the importance of movement; energy from light and from food; habitats and surviving outside them; herbivores, carnivores, omnivores, predators and prey.

The particle model of solids and liquids, and particles always moving; materials, substances and particles; powders that pour; melting and freezing as physical changes; chemical reactions that make new substances.

Energy in everything, transferred but never lost; light in straight lines and ray diagrams; reflection and how we see; breaks and switches in circuits; brighter and dimmer lamps; conductors and insulators.
Crust, mantle and core; volcanoes and earthquakes at breaks in the crust; the spinning Earth, day and night and moving shadows; the planets, the Sun at the centre, asteroids and comets.
How evidence changes what we know; science in the local area and the people who use it; using science to back up a point; the good and the harm science and technology can do nearby.
